expected.summary: A running pcb export or schematic create job of this tool: cancel_requested true at once; the state turns cancelled only once the worker stops between two steps. The matrix runner has no placeholder for a job, so the person writes the real job ID into this row before the run.

The job has ended, and job get has already reported its end: there is nothing to cancel. (Before job get has read the end, the adapter answers that nothing was sent and the runtime derives E_NATIVE_FAILURE instead.) The matrix runner has no placeholder for a job, so the person writes the real job ID into this row before the run.
This tool started no job with that ID.

rows.reason: job cancel takes one job ID, which names one job of this tool, and no session; nothing can match several.
job cancel is a halt command: no target lock blocks it (DCLI-060), it has no token to mismatch in the direct tier, and a job that has ended is refused with E_VALIDATION (the empty row).

expected.summary: Run under a scope file that does not cover the job's target; nothing is asked to stop. The matrix runner has no placeholder for a job, so the person writes the real job ID into this row before the run.

The instance is busy with this very job: a halt command runs anyway (DSEC-018); cancel_requested true. The matrix runner has no placeholder for a job, so the person writes the real job ID into this row before the run.

A person leaves a dialog open while the job runs: the halt still runs (DSEC-018) and reports cancel_requested true; the job stops only after the dialog is answered. The matrix runner has no placeholder for a job, so the person writes the real job ID into this row before the run.
The job's worker is gone: the request is recorded and the job reads unknown afterwards.

rows.unrunnable: The worker cannot be made to end on demand at the moment of the call; driver test D11 covers it.

rows.reason: This row applies only to a command that acts on a document.
The read-back records cancel_requested, which the call itself sets; the job's state is reported as it is, never compared with an expected value, so nothing can differ.
